title: quorum-based-consensus-for-noisy-canary-evaluations
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: Canary detectors in production increasingly face noisy signal environments (multi-tenant traffic, transient spikes, and heterogeneous tail behaviors). Simple single-metric thresholds or single-probe detectors either produce false positives during noise bursts or delay rollouts due to conservative thresholds. This PR adds a quorum-based consensus layer to the canary evaluation pipeline that: 1) requires a configurable quorum of independent signal partitions to agree on degradation, 2) progressively calibrates quorum strictness during low-signal windows, and 3) applies traffic-weighted voting so that partitions contributing more production traffic have proportionally larger influence.

Design summary: The new component (quorum_detector) acts as a final decision gate after individual detectors (latency delta, p95 drift, error-rate spike, throughput regression) emit per-partition verdicts. Key ideas: 
- Partitioning: requests are partitioned by top-level routing key (customer-id, region, or synthetic probe buckets). Each partition runs the existing per-partition detector.
- Voting model: each partition returns a vote: PASS, FAIL, or INSUFFICIENT. Votes are weighted by recent traffic share and smoothed by an exponential decay window.
- Quorum rules: a canary is flagged only when weighted FAIL vote >= quorum_threshold AND the number of consenting partitions >= quorum_count_min. Quorum thresholds are configurable per-canary.
- Progressive calibration: when overall sample counts are low, the detector relaxes quorum_count_min with a taper function and records increased uncertainty in telemetry. This avoids over-reacting to small-sample noise while surfacing the uncertainty signal to operators.
- Confidence tapering: an uncertainty score is attached to decisions; automated rollouts can opt into strict or permissive policies based on uncertainty.

Implementation details: 
- New runtime module: perf-canary/src/detectors/quorum_detector.rs (Rust). Handles vote aggregation, weighting, progressive calibration.
- Config schema: expanded canary config with fields: quorum_threshold, quorum_count_min, sample_decay_half_life_ms, uncertainty_policy (strict|permissive|auto). Documentation added in docs/design/quorum.md.
- Simulation harness: tests/sim/quorum_sim.py contains workload generators (multi-tenant Poisson, bursty spiky, correlated tail events) and an experiment driver to sweep quorum params and compare detection latency / false positive rate.
- Observability: emits metrics: quorum_votes_total, quorum_weighted_fail_ratio, quorum_uncertainty_score, quorum_decision_latency_ms, quorum_partitions_considered. Traces include per-partition vote bundles for offline debugging.

Results: In simulation on a corpus of historical traffic traces (internal dataset), tuned defaults reduce median false positive rate by ~46% on noisy multi-tenant traces while increasing median detection latency by +180ms (tradeoff configurable). On synthetic low-sample scenarios the progressive calibration prevented 92% of spurious rollbacks observed with previous detectors.

Backward compatibility & migration: Default quorum config is conservative (quorum_threshold=0.6, quorum_count_min=3, uncertainty_policy=auto) and preserves prior behavior for single-partition canaries. Existing canary configs are automatically upgraded with defaults; operators can opt-in to stricter policies.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added for aggregation edge cases (weighted ties, all-insufficient), property tests for decay behavior, and integration tests in the canary runner. A limited canary rollout will be staged under a feature flag: rollout-guard.quorum-enabled.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (docs/design/quorum.md)
- [x] Unit + property tests
- [x] Simulation harness + benchmark scripts
- [x] Metrics + tracing hooks
- [x] Upgrade path + backward-compatible defaults

Related work and references: This PR integrates with sentinel and rollout policies: it emits a quorum_decision event that the rollout orchestrator can use as a hard-fail or soft-fail (with uncertainty). See ENG-2684 for product acceptance criteria and SUP-452 for on-call guidance.

Notes: the PR intentionally separates quorum aggregation from signal detection so that new detectors (e.g., semantic-quality regressors) can plug into the voting model without rewriting decision logic.

review_comments: Ilya Ramirez: Can you explain how this interacts with the existing sentinel fallback? If quorum returns INSUFFICIENT, does sentinel auto-fallback or treat as pass?

Maya Thompson: Good question — INSUFFICIENT is surfaced as UNCERTAIN to sentinel. By default sentinel treats UNCERTAIN as pass for soft-rollouts and as fail for strict rollouts. I added a sentence in docs and a new field uncertainty_policy to make this explicit.
Samir Patel: The weighting by traffic share seems to bias towards noisy large customers. Can we cap per-partition weight to avoid a single tenant dominating?
Maya Thompson: Agree — implemented a per-partition weight cap (max_partition_weight_pct) with sensible default 0.4. Added tests demonstrating domination scenarios.
Ruth Chen: Simulation looks promising but please include a case with correlated region-wide spikes (network flaps) — might still cause coordinated failures.

Maya Thompson: Added correlated-spike generator and a mitigation note: we expose 'region-coordination-threshold' which requires failures across orthogonal partition keys (e.g., customer and region) to make a decision when enabled.
Ilya Ramirez: CI flaky job flaked once; reran integration-test and green. Approving after that.
Samir Patel: Approving — left small nit for log level on noisy events.
release_notes: Add quorum-based canary decisioning to reduce noisy false positives; configurable quorum and progressive calibration; metrics and tracing for debugging.
